title: Making an open schematically dense
statement:
Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $U\subseteq T$ a
quasi-compact open. There is a $U$-admissible blow-up $T'\to T$
([sk-def-nagata-admissible]) such that its inverse image of $U$ is
schematically dense in $T'$ and its complement is the support of an
effective Cartier divisor.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] to the given qcqs scheme $T$ and quasi-compact open $U$. Choose a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ with $V(\mathcal I)=T\setminus U$. These are exactly the hypotheses of Stacks Tag 01PH; no density of $U$ in $T$ is assumed.

On every affine open contained in $U$, [lemma-nagata-ideal-unit-off-support] identifies the ideal sections with the structure-ring sections. These affine opens form a basis of $U$, so $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$. Form $b:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$. Finite type, quasi-coherence and this restriction identity make $b$ a $U$-admissible blow-up by [sk-def-nagata-admissible].

source.place: First paragraph: choose the boundary ideal and blow it up

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] to $\mathcal I$. The extended ideal $\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor and defines an effective Cartier divisor $E\subseteq T'$. The only hypothesis of this principalization theorem beyond quasi-coherence is finite type, supplied in step 1.

The image-ideal definition [def-nagata-extended-ideal] identifies the support of $E$ with $b^{-1}(V(\mathcal I))$: on affine patches where $b$ is induced by $A\to B$, the ideal is $IB$, and a prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ contains $IB$ if and only if its contraction to $A$ contains $I$. Hence $|E|=b^{-1}(T\setminus U)=T'\setminus b^{-1}(U)$. Thus the divisor complement is exactly the inverse image of the specified open.

Apply [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense] to the effective Cartier divisor $E$ on $T'$. Its statement says that the complement is scheme-theoretically dense, namely the structure-sheaf map to the direct image from that complement is injective. By step 4 this complement is $b^{-1}(U)$, proving both required conclusions for the single blow-up $b$. No reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

To realize the unit's second paragraph, let $c:T''\to T'$ be any further $b^{-1}(U)$-admissible blow-up. By [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup], the extended effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{T''}$ is again effective Cartier. Its support is $c^{-1}(|E|)$ by the prime-ideal calculation in step 4, applied to $c$ and $\mathcal J$ using [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Consequently its complement is $c^{-1}(b^{-1}(U))$. Applying [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense] to this divisor proves that this complement is scheme-theoretically dense. For a finite tower $T_n\to\cdots\to T_0=T'$, induct on $n$ with invariant: the iterated extended ideal is effective Cartier with complement the inverse image of $b^{-1}(U)$, and that complement is schematically dense. Steps 3-5 give the base $n=0$. For the induction step apply the cited Cartier total-transform theorem to the ideal on $T_n$, the prime-containment calculation to $T_{n+1}\to T_n$, and the cited density theorem to the resulting divisor. The Cartier pullback theorem applies to every blow-up, so no additional assumption on the centers is used.
